newsitem.title: USA: Springfield, Mass. expected to OK $25 mln issue.
newsitem.headline: Springfield, Mass. expected to OK $25 mln issue.

text.p: The Springfield City Council was expected at a special meeting Tuesday evening to approve $25 million in general obligation bonds for the expansion of the basketball Hall of Fame.

"We're just putting it in place as a good faith measure for the Hall trustees," said Springfield's Treasurer Donna Williams, adding that officials do not expect Springfield taxpayers will ever have to cover the costs of that bonding.

A spokeswoman for the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame said its trustees want to see $25 million in public financing in place when they meet in the western Massachusetts city on Oct. 30 to take a final vote on the Hall's renovation. They have discussed moving the Hall of Fame to Orlando, Fla.

Williams said officials expect the state Legislature to complete action on a state bond authorization for the same amount by January - at which time Springfield's financial pledge will pledge will be withdrawn.
The City Council gave preliminary approval of the bonding on Aug. 12. There was no public opposition to the local promise of financing, a council staff member said Tuesday.
The renovation is part of a planned $88 million redevelopment of Springfield's Connecticut River waterfront. The complex would include retail outlets and a tourism center.
